title: Silo Standard v0 — silo.json
description: The manifest of a silo (silo-standard-v0.md). The schema freezes only vocabulary that a reference manifest exercises; designed pieces nothing exercises yet are proposed in proposed-extensions.md (party, proposal, mention/hand-off, automation templates, the Horizon strip, sensitive, more archetypes). Field classes: EVERY spec field in this schema is ADDITIVE (a kernel that does not understand one loads what it understands and lists the rest as wants); the RESTRICTIVE class (unknown ⇒ the install is refused) exists in the standard and is EMPTY in v0 — its first planned member is `sensitive` (annex). The `status` block is written only by the kernel and is not described here: it is not part of the file an author submits.

id.description: The silo id. Reserved: the kernel's words and the ids of silos already approved (they survive uninstall). The CONVENTION is not declared: the kernel derives it from the canonical root of each source and writes it in status.

icon.description: The silo's glyph, a name from the closed catalog (catalogs.md, Icons). The kernel draws it wherever the silo is named by a mark: the rail, its pages. Absent = the kernel's own silo glyph. A name, never an image: a manifest carries no UI.

kinds.description: Kinds are published qualified by the silo (invoices/invoice); here they carry no prefix because the prefix IS metadata.id.

relations.description: Typed relations between existing hubs that the KERNEL stores (<dataDir>/silos/<id>/relations.json), written by the owner. A silo with relations may have no sources, no kinds and no producer: it is an edge-only silo. For now: agent → agent only, cardinality one.

theme.description: Optional, declared: a LOOK the silo brings — colour values only, in the standard's closed vocabulary (catalogs.md «Theme tokens»), for light AND dark. The kernel checks its contrast at validation (conformance §12: a failing pair rejects the manifest); approving makes it AVAILABLE in Settings › Appearance beside the built-in looks — nothing changes on screen until someone chooses it, per browser. A theme never sets fonts, layout, status colours or the terminal palette. A silo whose only content is a theme is valid: no producer, sources or kinds.

name.description: The look's name in the picker («Heather»).

themeColor.description: #rrggbb only — no alpha, no names, no functions: a manifest carries values, never CSS.

themeMode.description: One mode of a theme: the closed token vocabulary (catalogs.md «Theme tokens»). An unknown token is an ERROR, not a want — a colour the kernel cannot place would be silently dropped. accent-soft is optional: absent, the kernel derives it from accent.

expression.description: Layer 1 of the language (expressions.md): field comparison, membership (in []), and/or, now ± duration, since(state), is human, startsWith. No aggregation — the aggregators (count/sum/max/all/any, one level, over sub-kinds or refs only) appear only in computed and in pulse.aggregate.

template.description: A template with {{field}} and {{a || b}} as a fallback chain.

label.description: Plain words for a state or a pulse term; the raw value is never painted.

role.description: The producer role; the approval dialog binds it to one or SEVERAL agents (the operator's level) and the binding lives in the operator store. 'any-agent' = any agent with the skill named in via.

via.description: The skill or mechanism through which it produces (e.g. team-plan).

protocol.description: The producer's rules (open/reopen/new, re-read before writing…). Prose: injected ONLY into the declared producers, in both engines.

sync.description: Only when the producer syncs from an outside service. Mechanical precondition: with ownerWritable fields, the silo validates only if the producer holds a bearer (it reads the merged view through the API).

contract.description: Minimum required: one record per file, idempotence, normalization (money {amount,currency}, ISO dates, canonical state), never over the owner's overlay.

stateMap.description: Table from exported value to canonical state; part of the producer's contract, not of the reader.

type.description: files: globs by convention. kernel: the data already lives in the kernel — the source names a kind of the kernel-kinds catalog and reads no one's files. In a kernel source type and root say the same thing and must match.

root.description: agent-state: expands under silos/<id>/ of EVERY agent (legacy exceptions are a closed list of the kernel, never a field here). project: over the project folders Silos knows; a worktree resolves to its main checkout. kernel: the kernel holds the records — no glob, no parser, no expects; the derived convention is kernel:<kind>.

kind.description: Only in a kernel source: the kind of the kernel-kinds catalog that the silo presents (catalogs.md «Kernel kinds», unprefixed — kernel names are reserved). A kind this kernel does not publish = the silo does not validate.

glob.description: The validator confines it to the location class of root: realpath, no .., no symlink escape, regular files only, size caps. A glob over the root of a project does not validate. From the resolved canonical root the kernel DERIVES the convention (one per source).

cadence.description: When the last write is older than this, EVERY slot of the silo says so (freshness).

envelope.description: The envelope: what every record maps. updatedBy may be declared absent (absent: unknown).

mustMatchField.description: Names under which the id may appear in the file; it must match the file name or the record does not parse (and the explanation says so).

charset.description: The charset of RECORD ids (per kind) — distinct from the charset of silo ids.

state.description: computed accepts aggregators over sub-kinds (all(tasks, state = done) ? done : active) — a kind with no state field of its own derives it from its children.

inherit.description: Sub-kinds without timestamps of their own inherit the parent's.

written.description: The value written on disk wins even when a formula exists (use it when the stored value is the truth — e.g. it records activity the formula cannot see — and the page's order depends on it).

mayBeEmpty.description: A record with no moment still reads (empty at): a plan without updatedAt is still a plan. Without it, a missing at makes the record unreadable.

hub.description: conversation only through a declared field or the owner's gesture (mention, v0.x); agent/folder come from the location. platform: platform data — the record belongs to no agent, folder or conversation (an account is not an agent); only a kernel source sustains it, and it is the DECLARED absence of a hub, not a fifth hub with a page. task (annex v0.x «task anchor»): the record hangs from a TASK of the plans silo — only `from: parent`, only over a kernel kind the catalog declares with parent `task` (execution): the kernel resolves the task and writes it; the manifest only presents it.

from.description: location: the hub comes from where the record lives. parent: the hub is the parent the kernel resolved for a kernel kind that declares one (hub task).

absent.description: The kind does not write it (plans): the envelope accepts it declared, never invented.

stamp.description: The timestamp field the kernel writes with «now» every time it stamps updatedBy = owner (set-field, append-item, move-item) — e.g. support's updatedAt, which the producer's reopen rule reads.

terminal.description: From this derive: what the pulse counts (the live states), Done today (the transition observed in the journal), board columns, fold, needs-you exclusions.

type.description: money = {amount: number, currency} already normalized (parsing localized strings is the producer's job). number = a finite JSON number with no unit (e.g. a usage window's percent); comparable with numeric literals, never summable in the pulse (sum is money only). actor = an agent id or a human name, soft resolution (enables `is human`). attachment = a path to a document, confined like the globs, opens in the viewer. refs(<sub-kind>) = ids of siblings (withinParent). object = a JSON object preserved as is, read only by a role (a task's wait {owner, action}): never a column, never compared.

empty.description: The value when missing or empty (never invents: '' or 'other' belong to the manifest, in plain sight).

fallback.description: A chain of fields to take the value from when it is missing.

anyOf.description: Conditional alias: accepted only when the value has the requested form; otherwise the explanation names the field and asks.

label.description: 21-11: the words the column header and the record page use for the field («memory», «started»). Voice only. A view's `at` is said with the label of the field the envelope maps it to.

unit.description: 21-11: only on a `number` field — the unit the cell says the number with («41.5 %», «312 MB»). Voice only: comparing and filtering stay on the number.

lift.description: Declarable structural tolerance: a loose field (or a string) is lifted into a minimal child record — empty, not invented. E.g. a case that carries only a loose threadId reads as one synthesized thread.

subKind.description: Child records inside the parent's file, with their own envelope anchored to the parent. NO derived surfaces by default (every note in ⌘K would be noise).

writeMerge.description: The discipline when writing an appendOnly sub-kind: union by keys + order (union(at,by,text) ordered by at).

envelope.description: The child's envelope; id/state/at/updatedBy optional (at may inherit from the parent; a child without states paints no board).

subKinds.description: The children of a child — e.g. the notes[] and conversations[] of a task. Two levels at most (record → child → grandchild); the validator refuses a third in plain words. Keys `<record>/<collection>/<child>/<collection>/<grandchild>`.

word.description: The word the row uses to say that future («resets» for a usage window; absent = «due»). Voice only: the role and its predicates do not change.

waitingOn.description: The field (of type object) holding the wait. The role reads from the raw object {owner, action?, asked?, options?} — asked: the question in words (string); options: 1–4 strings of up to 40 characters when the answer is a choice. Outside that shape asked/options are ignored and never invalidate the record (catalogs.md, task role).

releases.description: The sibling collection of conversations where the release verb marks a thread as released ({session, released}); the last entry of each thread, by position, decides whether it is current or past.

task.description: Which fields are the owner, the dependencies, the wait {owner, action}, the next check and the conversations of a task. With them the kernel computes — on request, never written — waiting, gate, stalled, stalledCause and stalledBy (the task flow), readable in predicates like any field. It reads the states by their standard names: pending, in_progress, in_review, blocked, done, cancelled; only done resolves a dependency.

roles.description: Field roles of the envelope (of a kind or a sub-kind). due: needs-you predicates and the Horizon strip. task: the flow of a task. party stays in the annex.

labelOverride.description: A state that READS differently under a predicate (done + notes startsWith 'Dropped:' → «dropped»).

unknownFields.description: Unknown fields are ALWAYS preserved (real producers write free-form fields beyond any contract). It is a const: there is no destructive mode.

computed.description: Derived ON READ over an index invalidated by mtime; never materialized; a field of the same name written on disk is ignored (except with at.written: authoritative) and the explanation names it.

ownerWritable.description: Fields set-field may write. Over a sync source they trigger the overlay by convention (seals the base value, retires when the source reaches it, contradiction → Needs you).

examples.description: Mandatory and SYNTHETIC (never personal data): the conformance fixture, the empty-state preview, the dry-run without records, and the worked example of the producer instructions.

relation.description: A typed edge between hubs. The kernel stores it, refuses in words a cycle (if acyclic) or a dangling id, and sets aside from the chain an edge whose agent is archived or deleted (it stays in the file, said).

cardinality.description: Each source points at one target at most.

acyclic.description: true: the kernel refuses the write that would close a cycle. A tree and a lens are declared only over an acyclic relation.

archetype.description: v0: the ones the reference manifests exercise. record is free for every kind (not declared). tree: roots = the ends with no outgoing edge, children by the relation named in `relation`. timeline/credentials/files enter with the migration that first uses them.

kind.description: A kind or kind/sub-kind (plan/task). A tree does not carry one: it draws a relation.

relation.description: Only in a tree: the relation (spec.relations[].name) it draws.

label.description: 21-11, optional: the view's name on its silo's page («Worktrees») — a silo with several list views over different kinds shows a switch between them by these names; the first view is the default.

21-11, optional: what the folded records are, in a few words on one line («ended or another user's») — the fold line says it beside its count («55 ended or another user's · Show»). Without it the page says «55 more».

groupBy.description: board: `state` (its columns). list (21-11): a dimension — a field, `agent`, `folder`, `project` or `state` — whose records go together under a heading with its count over the whole set; those with no value in a group of their own, the last, named («No conversation»). Contiguous across pages.

first.description: 21-11, list: what goes first — the mirror of fold (a predicate, never a hidden order). With groupBy, a group that holds one goes earlier. After that, the most recent.

surfaces.description: Grants — what the approval dialog lists and the operator switches off per slot. The derived surfaces (⌘K, record, hubs strip, sidebar-glyph) are not requested: they emerge from the envelope.

field.description: Required with sum; must be money. Different currencies = separate terms, never summed.

pulse.description: A count or sum over live states (derived from terminal) and the COMPLETE set; the order between silos is the operator's and the kernel folds the excess.

clears.description: The dispatchable condition that clears the item. An unconditional blocking does not validate; the operator may raise an item to blocking when the author falls short, never the other way round.

audience.description: Whom the entry speaks to. Absent = owner. producer-agent: routine rows go to the bound producer — the owner's inbox does not list them; the grant is the OPERATOR's (approving a manifest that declares it, revocable per entry through audienceOff), requires a bound producer and a condition that producer can clear (conformance §7), and never on blocking (what blocks is the owner's by definition).

lens.description: Groups or folds an existing surface (a kernel floor that cannot be negotiated away). Folds, never hides: what blocks, what is escalated and what is ready for the owner is painted unfolded above any group; what falls in no group goes to a group of its own, never out. Shown as a chip that switches off in one click.

over.description: The surface it groups. For now: the tasks view.

relation.description: An acyclic agent → agent relation of this silo.

by.description: subtree: one group per root, with everything that hangs from it.

verb.description: v0 = the verbs the reference manifests use. re-anchor, hand-off and create-automation enter with the annex piece that first uses them. kernel-verb (21-11, System 0.2.0, additive within v0): a mutation by the KERNEL of its own records, declared and visible as such — only over a kernel source, `name` from an ENUMERATED, closed catalog (catalogs.md «Kernel-verbs»; v0: stop-process) that the kernel kind admits, `kind` the kind that presents it, `when` optional; always an owner gesture. move-item: destination-before-source and idempotent retry are fixed semantics of the verb. ensure-record: ensures ONE reserved record (id) of a top-level kind in a known location — born from its seed when missing, never overwrites one that exists — and, with rotate, moves its old finished children to a file that is not read as live. claim and release (additive within v0): claim adds an id to the identity collection `link` of the subKind (idempotent) and applies `set` in the SAME write; release appends a mark to the releases collection (`link` = roles.task.releases) and never rewrites one; with `dispose` the same write disposes the task's state.

name.description: kernel-verb: the name of the kernel verb it declares (a closed catalog: stop-process). A name the kernel does not know rejects the manifest.

when.description: kernel-verb: a predicate (expressions.md) over the record — when the page offers the door. The kernel's own guard (the boolean field the catalog names, e.g. stoppable) is checked at the gesture all the same.

link.description: claim/release: the subKind collection the verb acts on (claim: an identity collection — a task's conversations[]; release: the collection of roles.task.releases).

set.description: claim: the fields (with declared states) the verb sets in the same write — plans: {status: in_progress}.

keep.description: claim: declared states that `set` never overwrites — with the task in one of them the claim links the id and leaves the state as it is (plans: [blocked], a wait still open).

dispose.description: release (additive within v0): the task's disposition on release. Only if the record is in `from` at write time AND the released thread was the last current one, the SAME write of the mark sets `field` to the requested state (one of `allowed`) or to `default` when none is requested; in any other case the state is untouched and the response says `kept`. `field` is the subKind's state field; `from`, `default` and `allowed` are declared states. `set` stays forbidden on release.

id.description: ensure-record: the reserved id of the record it ensures (plans: tasks).

seed.description: ensure-record: the value the record is born with; it must read with the manifest.

rotate.description: ensure-record: monthly rotation of the standing record. When it is ensured in a new month, the children that match `when` (and that no staying child names through `keepReferencedBy`) are written to `into` ({{month}} = the month being closed, YYYY-MM; union by id if it exists, never overwritten) BEFORE they leave the record; their ids are noted in `retired` (never reused) and `stamp` keeps the month.

undated.description: Inside THIS `when`, a since(…) with no recorded transition (null — the journal's baseline) counts as old. Outside the rotation a null since stays false (expressions.md).

by.description: task-owner: the agent that roles.task.owner names in THAT record — only on claim and release.

templates.description: Pre-written messages; every templated message carries its provenance («composed from record X via silo Y»).
